segments: ... and the Arabs acted treacherously,
and imprisoned two thousand five hundred Frankish men, merchants and sailors who were in it;
and they made the excuse that the period of the truce had expired.
Then the Franks went out to a city on the shore of the Red Sea called Ayla (Eilat);
and they prepared many ships and boats, and sailed in the Red Sea,
where from of old no man had ever said that Franks had sailed in the Red Sea.
And they captured many Arab ships
which were full of great wealth,
and they killed a great multitude of the people of the city called Aydhab.
Saladin sent ships from Alexandria on the loads of camels,
and they launched them into the Red Sea.
And the Arabs {OCR: ܛܝܝ̈ܐ for ܛܢܝ̈ܐ} overtook the Franks,
and on both sides many were killed.
And in the year 1494
of the Greeks [1182/1183 AD]:
Andronikos, a man from the nobles of the Greeks,
the one whom King Manuel had expelled from Constantinople,
persuaded the young Alexios and his mother,
and entered Constantinople again,
and for a short time showed submission.
Then he threw the mother of the youth, her daughter, and her son-in-law into the sea;
and Alexios the youth himself he destroyed secretly.
And he killed more than a thousand nobles,
and burned [them] with fire,
and gouged out the eyes of many.
And as for the young woman, the wife of Alexios, that impure old man took her as his wife.
And he expelled the Franks from Constantinople.
Those [Franks], when they went out,
burned fourteen thousand monasteries and villages in the territories of the Greeks.
And the king of Sicily also came,
and demolished and devastated many of the cities of the Greeks.
And in the year
578 of the Arabs [1182/1183 AD]:
Saladin went out from Egypt and came to Damascus,
and from there to Aleppo,
and he wished to make war against it.
Then one of the nobles advised him
that he should first cross the Euphrates,
and take control over the cities of Mesopotamia and Assyria,
and then he would easily be able to take it.
And having accepted his advice,
he crossed the Euphrates,
and came against Edessa and captured it,
and likewise also Harran.
And he went further to Callinicus (Raqqa) and captured it.
And from there he went to Araban,
and its guards brought down its keys to him, and he took it, and along with it also Maksin.
And he showed kindness to the people of Khabur {OCR: ܒܢܝ̈ for ܒܙ̈}.
